thread:
alex.k: FYI Brightline is hitting sustained 429s on their Dedicated cluster since ~09:15 UTC. They say it correlates with long-context user sessions. Can we triage?

maria: Seeing the alert, grabbing logs from the node pool now.

devon: Quick snapshot from the runtime logs (09:12-09:20):
```
[09:12:03] model-serving: WARN kv_eviction: eviction_rate=0.78, free_mem_pct=6.1, cause=long_contexts
[09:13:20] auth: INFO request=abc123 status=429 route=/v1/generate tenant=brightline
[09:14:05] runtime: ERROR alloc_fail: slab_fragmentation=0.67, alloc_retry=false
[09:15:11] autoscaler: INFO scale_decision=none reason="no_headroom_due_to_fragmentation"
[09:16:34] model-serving: WARN kv_eviction: eviction_type=prefix_kv, evicted_items=1423
```

samir: Eviction + high slab fragmentation = KV cache thrash. Autoscaler didn't spin because nodes still report used_mem below threshold, but fragmentation prevented useful allocation.

alex.k: Customer logs show repeated long-context requests (20-30k tokens) from a small set of users. They said this started after a feature rollout earlier this week.

maria: Repro steps I used locally (quick):
```bash
# simulate long sessions hitting tenant on dedicated cluster
for i in {1..20}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $BRIGHTLINE_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"'$(python -c 'print("x "+"y "*10000)')'","max_tokens":2000}' &

done
```
Result: eviction_rate spikes then later 429s on subsequent requests.

devon: Root cause hypothesis: long-prefix KV usage + fragmentation + aggressive prefix caching leads to repeated evictions. Evictions cause extra allocations, increasing fragmentation until allocator refuses further large allocations and the runtime returns 429s as a protective throttle.

samir: Immediate mitigations:
- Ask Brightline to drop max_context (short-term) or use streaming smaller chunks.
- Increase kv_cache_size on their dedicated config (temporary increase) to absorb active prefixes.
- Add a soft rate limit on long-context routes at the API gateway for that tenant.

alex.k: I'll message account team to apply soft rate limit and ask customer to throttle long sessions. Maria/D: can we push a config change to bump kv_cache_size for the dedicated pool?

maria: I can change the tenant config to bump kv_cache_size +10% for the pool. Will monitor eviction_rate.

devon: Long-term fixes:
- Improve slab consolidation on allocator engineer backlog (ticket filed).
- Add fragmentation metrics to cluster SLO dashboards.
- Consider proactive fallback to smaller model-variant when fragmentation high.

ops-bot: ACTION CREATED: ticket #RINF-5821 "allocator slab consolidation - fragmentation mitigation" assigned to eng-runtime.

samir: I also recommend adjusting autoscaler to consider fragmentation-weighted headroom so scale triggers when fragmentation is high even if raw used_mem is below threshold.

alex.k: Update for the thread: applied soft rate limit at 09:37 UTC, bumped tenant kv_cache_size at 09:42. Brightline reports error rate dropping to normal by 09:55.

maria: Post-mortem notes to include: repro script, sample runtime logs (attached above), and suggested tenant best-practices doc (limit >10k token sessions).

devon: I'll link the perf test we used and a short checklist for support ops: 1) check eviction_rate, 2) check slab_fragmentation, 3) consider temp kv bump, 4) apply rate limit.

samir: Closing loop: agree on schedule for allocator ticket and autoscaler tuning. Will follow up in eng-runtime channel once a patch is available.

alex.k: Thanks team. I'll ping account/CS to confirm Brightline OK with the temporary config and confirm they won't rollback feature that created the spike.

maria: Confirmed with customer at 10:05 UTC — they accepted temporary kv bump and will gate the rollout.

alex.k: Marking thread resolved for now. We should still track RINF-5821. :white_check_mark:
